rich_summary: This section centers on the public rise of Karna and the beginning of Drona’s long‑planned revenge against King Drupada. When Kripa demands Karna declare his royal lineage before fighting Arjuna, Duryodhana immediately crowns him king of Anga so that the duel may proceed. Karna gratefully pledges eternal friendship, sealing the famous alliance between the two men. The moment turns emotional when Karna’s foster father, the charioteer Adhiratha, enters and embraces him; Bhima mocks Karna’s low birth, but Duryodhana fiercely defends him, arguing that valor—not lineage—defines a warrior. Later, Drona demands his pupils capture Drupada as their teacher’s fee. The Kauravas attack first but are routed by Drupada, until the Pandavas—led by Bhima’s brute force and Arjuna’s unmatched archery—enter the battle and begin turning the tide. The chapter highlights themes of social status, loyalty, and the emerging rivalry among the heroes.

highlight_spans.why: Kunti regains consciousness and sees her sons prepared for battle, capturing her helpless fear as a mother watching events she cannot stop.
Kripa’s demand that Karna reveal his lineage establishes the central conflict about birth versus merit that defines Karna’s story.
Adhiratha’s emotional embrace of Karna after the coronation humanizes Karna and reveals the deep bond with the man who raised him.
Duryodhana’s defense of Karna argues that greatness can arise from unknown origins, expressing a powerful thematic challenge to rigid caste pride.
Drona demands Drupada’s capture as his teacher’s fee, launching the military expedition that reveals the true abilities of the Kuru princes.

top_scenes.scene_text: Duryodhana crowns Karna king of Anga in the arena as priests chant, a golden umbrella held above Karna while astonished warriors and princes watch.
The old charioteer Adhiratha rushes into the arena and tearfully embraces the newly crowned Karna, whose head is still wet with coronation water.
Bhima storms into the Panchala army with a massive mace, smashing war elephants while Arjuna’s arrows streak across the battlefield behind him.
